# Bodies — Canon RF full-frame vs RF-S APS-C

**Dimension:** Canon mirrorless body lineup, sensor format, weight, stabilization,
and beginner/travel/family/macro suitability. Source details in
[citations.md](../citations.md). See [glossary](../glossary.md) for terms.

## Sensor format in one line

Canon mirrorless splits into **APS-C** (smaller sensor, 1.6× crop, lighter,
cheaper) and **full-frame** (larger sensor, better low light and background
blur, heavier, pricier) [[11]](../citations.md#c11)[[12]](../citations.md#c12).
On APS-C, multiply a lens's focal length by **1.6** for its
full-frame-equivalent view [[28]](../citations.md#c28).

## R7 weight — contradiction resolved

Sources circulated both ~375 g and ~530 g for the R7. These are not in conflict:
**530 g is body-only, 612 g is CIPA (with battery + card)**; the stray "375 g"
was cross-contamination from the R50's weight
[[4]](../citations.md#c4)[[9]](../citations.md#c9)[[10]](../citations.md#c10).

## Budget tiers

- **Entry (~$429–900):** R100, R50, R10 — all APS-C, all **no IBIS**.
- **Mid (~$1,099–1,449):** R8 (full-frame, no IBIS), R7 (APS-C, has IBIS).
- **Pro (~$1,799+):** R6 Mark II, R5 Mark II — full-frame, IBIS, weather-sealed.

Notable beginner tension: the cheapest bodies skip IBIS, and Canon's small
budget primes also lack lens IS — so the cheapest combos have **no
stabilization at all** for handheld low-light/macro
[[4]](../citations.md#c4)[[24]](../citations.md#c24).

## Suitability by use-case

- **Travel (lightweight priority):** R50 (375 g) or R8 (461 g). The R8 is
  full-frame yet only 86 g heavier than the APS-C R50 — weight is driven more
  by the lens than the body [[1]](../citations.md#c1)[[2]](../citations.md#c2)
  (see [kit-weight](kit-weight.md)).
- **Family (indoors, low light, kids moving):** full-frame low-light + fast AF
  favor R8 or R6 II; IBIS on the R6 II helps handheld
  [[3]](../citations.md#c3).
- **Macro (later):** IBIS materially helps handheld close-ups, pointing to
  **R7** (APS-C, 8-stop IBIS, +1.6× reach) or **R6 II**; cheaper bodies work
  but lean on a tripod/flash [[4]](../citations.md#c4)[[40]](../citations.md#c40).

## Counter-perspectives

- **Full-frame may not be worth it for a beginner:** APS-C is "enough" for many,
  and the cheapest full-frame (R8) omits IBIS, which competitors include at
  similar prices [[13]](../citations.md#c13)[[2]](../citations.md#c2).
- **Overheating:** R8 has user-reported overheating in warm conditions during
  extended 4K video [[19]](../citations.md#c19).
- **RF-S lens ecosystem is thin:** Canon makes few native RF-S lenses, so APS-C
  buyers often mount heavier full-frame RF glass anyway — eroding the APS-C
  weight advantage [[63]](../citations.md#c63) (see
  [third-party-lenses](third-party-lenses.md)).

## Gaps and limitations

- All weights/prices are corroborated across DPReview spec database + secondary
  sources; Canon's own spec pages were anti-bot-blocked to direct fetch, so
  figures are spec-database-sourced, not read off canon.com in-session.
- Prices fluctuate; figures are mid-2026 street estimates, not fixed MSRP.
- An EOS R7 Mark II was rumored for ~2026 but is **not** confirmed shipping;
  not included as a recommendation. (Rumor-tier, excluded.)
